removal-warning-webhooks: Removing webhooks is irreversible and all incoming webhooks will be rejected.
add-code-host-connection-webhook: Please add a code host connection in order to create a webhook.
incoming-webhooks-description: Use incoming webhooks to notify Sourcegraph of code changes or changeset events.
no-webhooks-created-message: No webhooks have been created so far.
tokens-access-sourcegraph-api: Tokens may be used to access the Sourcegraph API with the full privileges of the token's creator.
global-settings-description: Global settings apply to all organizations and users. Settings for a user or organization override global settings.
user-feedback-survey-description: After using Sourcegraph for a few days, users are presented with a request to answer "How likely is it that you would recommend Sourcegraph to a friend?" on a scale from 0–10 and to provide some feedback. Responses are visible below (and are also sent to Sourcegraph).
syncing-repositories-message: Syncing repositories. It may take a few moments to clone and index each repository. Repository statuses are displayed below.
repositories-synced-from-code-hosts: Repositories are synced from connected <0>code host connections</0> .
create-issue-public-tracker: <0>Create an issue on the public issue tracker</0> , and include a description of the bug along with the info below (with secrets redacted). If the report contains sensitive information that should not be public, email the report to <1>support@sourcegraph.com</1>  instead.
redact-secrets-before-sharing: Please redact any secrets before sharing, whether on the public issue tracker or with support@sourcegraph.com.
slow-requests-log-description: This is the log of recent slow GraphQL requests received by the Sourcegraph instance. Handy for seeing what's happening between clients and our API.
copy-request-button-description: button will copy the GraphQL request as a cURL command in your clipboard. You will need to have $ACCESS_TOKEN set in your environment or to replace it in the copied command.
slow-requests-capture-configuration: Slow requests capture is configured through <0>site config</0>:

packages-synced-from-code-hosts: Packages are synced from connected <0>code hosts</0>.
organization-description: An organization is a set of users with associated configuration. See <0>Sourcegraph documentation</0> for information about configuring organizations.
recent-external-requests-log-description: This is the log of recent external requests sent by the Sourcegraph instance. Handy for seeing what's happening between Sourcegraph and other services.
list-updates-every-five-seconds: The list updates every five seconds.
outbound-request-logging-disabled: Outbound request logging is currently disabled.
enable-logging-in-site-config: to a non-zero value in your <0>site config</0> to enable it.
onboarding-task-list-description: This settings controls the onboarding task list that is displayed to all users by default.
no-requests-received: No requests received yet. Be sure to <0>configure the webhook on the code host</0> .
setup-github-webhook: To set up a GitHub webhook, follow the instructions below, or see more in the <0>GitHub webooks documentation</0>.
github-app-webhooks-note: Note: For GitHub App integrations, webhooks are created automatically. You do not need to create them manually.
github-settings-webhook-setup: On GitHub, go to the settings page of your organization. From there, click <0>Settings</0>, then <1>Webhooks</1>, then <2>Add webhook</2>.
payload-url-description: Payload URL: the URL you just copied above.
content-type-requirement: Content type: this must be set to <0>application/json</0>.
secret-token-description: Secret: the secret token you can find above.
select-events-description: Which events: select <0>Let me select individual events</0>, and then enable:
confirm-webhook-listing: Confirm that the new webhook is listed.
initial-ping-event: You should see an initial ping event sent from GitHub in the webhook logs above.
setup-gitlab-webhook: To set up a GitLab webhook, follow the instructions in the <0>GitLab integration documentation</0>.
setup-bitbucket-server-webhook: To set up a Bitbucket Server webhook, follow the instructions in the <0>Bitbucket Server integration documentation</0> .
setup-bitbucket-cloud-webhook: To set up a Bitbucket Cloud webhook, follow the instructions in the <0>Bitbucket Cloud integration documentation</0> .
setup-azure-devops-webhook: To set up an Azure DevOps webhook, follow the instructions in the <0>Azure DevOps integration documentation</0> .
gitservers-overview-description: Overview of all gitserver instances, on which this Sourcegraph instance stores source code.
checking-for-updates: Checking for updates... (reload in a few seconds)
schema-drift-detected: Schema drift is detected. Please resolve schema drift before attempting an upgrade.
learn-more-migrator: Learn more about the migrator <0>upgrade command</0>.
oob-migrations-completion: Some oob migrations must complete before a multi version upgrade can finish. Learn more at the <0>migrations</0> page, and reach out to <1>Sourcegraph support</1>  for clarifications.

no-pending-oob-migrations: There are no pending out-of-band migrations that need to complete.
feature-flags-description: Feature flags, as opposed to experimental features, are intended to be strictly short-lived. They are designed to be useful for A/B testing, and the values of all active feature flags are added to every event log for the purpose of analytics. To learn more, refer to <0>How to use feature flags</0> .
feature-flag-settings-management: Feature flag settings are managed by Sourcegraph and will be overridden by updates. Contact support for help.
out-of-band-migrations-description: Out-of-band migrations run in the background of the Sourcegraph instance convert data from an old format into a new format. Consult this page prior to upgrading your Sourcegraph instance to ensure that all expected migrations have completed.
contact-support-migration-error: <0>Contact support.</0> The following migrations are not in the expected state. You have partially migrated or un-migrated data in a format that is incompatible with the currently deployed version of Sourcegraph. <1>Continuing to run your instance in this state will result in errors and possible data loss.</1>
migration-completion-warning: The next version of Sourcegraph removes support for reading an old data format. Your Sourcegraph instance must complete the following migrations to ensure your data remains readable. <0>If you upgrade your Sourcegraph instance now, you may corrupt or lose data.</0>
contact-support-migration-progress: Contact support if these migrations are not making progress or if there are associated errors.
previous-version-migration-warning: The previous version of Sourcegraph does not support reading data that has been migrated into a new format. Your Sourcegraph instance must undo the following migrations to ensure your data can be read by the previous version. <0>If you downgrade your Sourcegraph instance now, you may corrupt or lose data.</0>
contact-support-downgrade-assistance: Contact support for assistance with downgrading your instance.
migration-end-version: and will cease running in v
background-jobs-description: This page lists <0>all running jobs</0> , their routines, recent runs, any errors, timings, and stats.
job-definition: <0>Job</0>: a bag of routines, started when the Cody app is launched
routine-definition: <0>Routine</0>: a background process that repeatedly executes its task indefinitely, using an interval passed at start
run-definition: <0>Run</0>: a single execution of a routine's task
host-definition: <0>Host</0>: a Sourcegraph instance that starts some jobs when launched
instance-definition: <0>Instance</0>: a job ran on a host
sourcegraph-ping-description: Sourcegraph periodically sends a ping to Sourcegraph.com to help our product and customer teams. It sends only the high-level data below. It never sends code, repository names, usernames, or any other specific data.
no-recent-ping-data: No recent ping data to display.
critical-telemetry-description: Critical telemetry includes only the high-level data below required for billing, support, updates, and security notices. This cannot be disabled.
